title: Fast Stream and Beyond Boundaries: Evaluation, Benchmarking, and Evidence
description:
The key requirements of this project are as follows:
- Workstream 1: Process evaluation relating to understand the role of Activity Managers (AMs) on Fast Stream, and their L&D and support requirements
- Workstream 2: Process evaluation to understand the skills and behaviours developed by Fast Streamers (including aligning with programme gaps, and updating the ToC)

- Workstream 5: Rapid Evidence Assessment on "What Works" in interventions similar to Fast Stream and Beyond Boundaries

title: Provision of MHR People First HR and Payroll Software and Associated Services
description:
Havant and South Downs College intends to enter into a call-off contract with Softcat plc for MHR People First, an integrated cloud HR and native payroll platform, together with associated implementation, hosting and support services.
The platform will support a single employee record, HR and payroll administration, employee and manager self-service, workflow automation and workforce reporting.
The scope comprises People First HR Hub, Payroll, Talent, LearnNow and Data Explorer (Core HR and Absence); the Pension Data Solution (LGPS and MDC); single sign-on and Active Directory synchronisation; hosting and maintenance; configuration, implementation, data migration and parallel payroll runs; training; the MHR Assist programme; and support and service desk. Pricing is based on approximately 800 employees plus 50 casual staff. Recruitment & Onboarding, Learning (LXP), BYOBI and RightCheck screening are excluded from this award.

The service will also equip parents/carers, and professionals with the tools and knowledge to support children with illnesses or Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND). This includes delivering direct interventions in line with a Child's Education, Health, and Care Plan (EHCP), as well as offering indirect support through professional training and parent/carer guidance. This provision will work across Young Hackney, Youth Justice Virtual School, Schools, and Early Years provision.
This contract will include for the provision of Speech and Language Therapists as part of the Hackney Experts at Hand team, in line with requirements related to the Department for Education's Experts at Hand initiative. title: CHS - Acute Electronic Patient Record (EPR) Contract Extension
description:
Croydon Health Services NHS Trust intends to extend its existing contract with Oracle Health for the provision of its acute Electronic Patient Record (EPR) system for a further three years, with an option to extend for an additional 12 months.

The extension will maintain continuity of the Trust’s existing clinical digital services, including the core EPR software, application management, hosting and associated support services. The existing system is integral to the Trust's clinical workflows and digital infrastructure, with significant technical dependencies and integration requirements.

The proposed arrangements include the removal of certain existing functionality and the introduction of additional integrated functionality, including Blood Transfusion Administration and Milk Management modules, to support the Trust's clinical and operational requirements. These modules require integration with the existing EPR environment, making technical compatibility, interoperability and continuity of clinical services key considerations.

title: FA08-14 Chemical Dosing
description:
The scope of the frameworks allows for a number of suppliers to provide Chemical Dosing services and expertise in relation to off-site build, minor site works and temporary hire.
Lot 1 - Off-site Build - 
The scope includes the survey, design, manufacture, testing and supply of package plant dosing systems, incorporating chemical storage and dosing equipment housed within GRP or alternative material kiosks, together with associated building services. 
Lot 2A - Northumbrian Water Operating Region and Lot 2B Essex & Suffolk Operating Region - 
The scope includes the provision of low-complexity and minor works services for existing chemical dosing and related assets across the North East and Essex & Suffolk operating regions. This includes refurbishment, modification, relocation and ad hoc maintenance activities at water and wastewater treatment facilities, pumping stations, boreholes and service reservoirs. Suppliers will provide the expertise and resources required to support the ongoing operation and performance of existing assets, delivering works efficiently and cost-effectively while supporting innovation and carbon reduction objectives.

title: NHS Over 40 Health Checks  General Practice Model of delivery
description:
Intention to Award Notice under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR) - Direct Award Process B
The awarding of this contract is subject to the Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023. For the avoidance of doubt, the Procurement Act 2023 and the Public Contracts Regulations 2015 do not apply to this award. 
 North Lincolnshire Council has determined that the proposed provider meets the relevant  criteria  set out in the Regulations. The Council is therefore satisfied that the provider is capable of delivering the proposed contract to the required standard. 
 The contract is for the provision of NHS Health Checks to eligible adults aged between 40 and 74 who are not currently on a cardiovascular disease register or being treated as being at risk of cardiovascular disease. 
 The service will be delivered through a General Practice service model within Primary Care settings. 
 The contract will be awarded to the eligible providers in accordance with Direct Award Process B under the Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023.

description: Timeliness of variable signs and signals (VSS) settings is one of our company's performance indicators. A KPMG review of our SRUS performance recommended measuring the quality of VSS settings to help identify how we can improve scores. title: Testing the effect of behavioural interventions on agri-environment scheme optio
description:
Testing the effect of behavioural interventions on agri-environment scheme option selection

This project follows a series of Choice Architecture Tests (CATs) that have been commissioned by Defra's Farming Directorate Behavioural Science and Analytics team. These CATs have tested various interventions in a hypothetical agri-environment scheme application environment to understand their effect on option selection. Key findings include:

• CAT 1 : tested the effect of defaults (pre-selected actions) on a hypothetical Sustainable Farming Incentive (SFI) application. Results showed a statistically significant increase in the environmental quality of the agreement generated through defaults compared to the current SFI application design.
• CAT 2 : tested the effect of defaults and guided selection on a hypothetical Countryside Stewardship (CS) mid-tier application. Results for CAT 2 also showed defaults being effective. The site has been operational since September 2024, with Treatment Pond 1 (TP1) brought online in accordance with planning conditions. 

Contaminated mine water has been entering TP1 at a controlled flow rate. Since commissioning, the passive treatment system has successfully removed an dissolved zinc from the inflowing mine water. 

The next stage of commissioning involves a structured optimisation programme aimed at enhancing treatment performance at Nent Haggs and informing the development of future passive mine water treatment systems for the Mining Remediation Authority.
